skill.name: personal-finance-visualizer
skill.description: Turn user-provided personal finance records into a local interactive report with spending, income, transfers and cash movement in English or Chinese. Use for statement-based finance charts and period comparisons, not bank-account actions or investment advice.
skill.summary: Create a local, interactive view of spending, income, transfers, and cash movement from user-provided records.
skill.author: jasonhmy

security_audit.summary: All 68 static findings are false positives based on the cited source context. The skill validates user-supplied records, renders a local report, and limits its update check to explicit metadata-only requests; no prompt injection or financial-data exfiltration evidence was found.

remediation.issue: The explicit update checker performs an external request.
remediation.suggestion: Keep update checks opt-in and document the destination, request data, timeout, and failure behavior.

remediation.issue: The report can write an exported HTML file containing transaction details.
remediation.suggestion: Retain explicit export consent, restrictive file permissions, non-overwrite behavior, and the warning that exports contain private data.

remediation.issue: Minified JavaScript and CSS trigger obfuscation heuristics.
remediation.suggestion: Publish source maps or formatted source alongside the maintained assets so reviewers can verify the interface more easily.

content.value_statement: Turn transaction records into a clear view of spending, income, transfers, and cash movement. Review charts locally without connecting bank accounts or requesting investment advice.
actual_capabilities: Validate normalized JSON or CSV transaction records.
Separate spending, income, refunds, transfers, and internal movements.
Apply confirmed personal shares, full refunds, and transfer settlements.
Render interactive spending, income, transfer, and cash-flow charts.
Serve the report on loopback or export it to a user-selected local path.
Show reports in English or Simplified Chinese.
limitations: It does not connect to banks or perform payments.
It does not provide investment, tax, or financial planning advice.
It does not include a universal PDF statement parser.
Results depend on complete, correctly classified source records.

use_cases.title: Review Monthly Spending
use_cases.description: Inspect category totals, personal shares, refunds, and daily spending for a selected period.

use_cases.title: Reconcile Shared Costs
use_cases.description: Separate personal spending from shared expenses and keep unresolved classifications visible.

use_cases.title: Audit Cash Movement
use_cases.description: Compare income, outgoing transfers, repayments, refunds, and internal account movements.
use_cases.target_user: Analysts preparing a private cash-flow review

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Report
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the personal finance visualizer with my normalized transaction records. Show the report in English for the full covered period.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Two Periods
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a local report from these records. Compare spending, income, transfers, and net cash movement by month. Keep unresolved items visible.

prompt_templates.title: Review Shared Expenses
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare a Simplified Chinese report from these normalized records. Apply only the confirmed personal shares and full refund mappings, then identify remaining review items.

prompt_templates.title: Export a Private Report
prompt_templates.prompt: Validate this dataset, render an English report for the requested dates, and export it only to my absolute path. Confirm coverage and unresolved items.

output_examples.input: A three-month normalized transaction dataset with salary, rent, groceries, a matched refund, and an internal transfer.
output_examples.output: A local interactive report with spending rings, income totals, transfer metrics, daily trends, refund status, and transaction details.

output_examples.input: A CSV export with dates, signed amounts, categories, and USD selected as the currency.
output_examples.output: A validated cash-flow report showing inflow, outflow, net change, category spending, and the covered date range.

output_examples.input: Shared household records with confirmed personal shares and one unresolved incoming payment.
output: Shared expenses are reduced to the confirmed personal share.
The unresolved incoming payment remains classified as a transfer.
The report notes the remaining item for review.

best_practices: Normalize dates, signs, currencies, and transaction identifiers before rendering.
Confirm refund and transfer matches using source evidence.
Review coverage, unresolved items, and exported-file privacy before sharing.
anti_patterns: Do not provide bank credentials or ask the skill to connect an account.
Do not treat unknown incoming money as income without confirmation.
Do not claim complete financial coverage from a partial statement export.

faq.question: Does this skill connect to my bank?
faq.answer: No. It processes records that you provide and does not connect to bank accounts.

faq.question: Can it parse any PDF statement?
faq.answer: No. PDF extraction depends on the available tools and the statement format.

faq.question: Where does the report run?
faq.answer: The default report runs on a loopback address and keeps the report in process memory.

faq.question: Can I export the report?
faq.answer: Yes. Export requires an explicit local path and creates a new HTML file containing transaction details.

faq.question: Does it give financial advice?
faq.answer: No. It summarizes supplied records and does not provide investment, tax, or financial planning advice.

faq.question: Which languages are supported?
faq.answer: The report supports English and Simplified Chinese.
